evidence: docs/adr/0014-inbound-webhook-auth.md:43-52 replaces the prior 'SECONDARY — URL-embedded token' decision and 'Receiver-side validation (S4b)' with a new tokenless design, and lines 59-64 delete the 'Single secret, single rotation path' and 'DEPENDENCY ON S5' consequences

docs/adr/0042-auto-lander.md:3 shows the repository correction method: a '> Superseded by ...' annotation that keeps the prior decision text intact
advisory.finding: ADR 0014's decision substance was rewritten in place: the title, Decision item 2 (the SECONDARY URL-embedded token control), item 3 (receiver-side validation), and the Consequences (including 'Single secret, single rotation path' and the 'DEPENDENCY ON S5' invariant) were replaced/deleted while Status remains 'Accepted', erasing the earlier decision instead of preserving it through a supersession notice, annotation, erratum, or replacement ADR.
scenarios: A future contributor reads ADR 0014 to understand why the earlier URL-token design existed and finds no record of the superseded decision or its S5 replication invariant

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update the app.py comments (lines 74-75 and 202-203) to reflect that the Gerrit webhooks plugin cannot send X-Rebar-Token and that the internal path is authenticated by X-Origin-Url.
evidence: src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:74-75: "Gerrit's ``webhooks`` plugin can send this via its ``header`` config (see infra/gerrit/webhooks.config)"
src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:202-203: "a legacy caller (a Gerrit webhook whose ``webhooks.config`` has not yet been re-pushed to send the header) keeps authenticating"

infra/gerrit/webhooks.config diff removes 'header = X-Rebar-Token: __BOT_TOKEN__' and states 'The deployed plugin also ignores arbitrary `header =` keys', and docs/adr/0014-inbound-webhook-auth.md:20-22 confirms the plugin does not read arbitrary header keys
advisory.finding: Code comments in app.py still assert Gerrit's webhooks plugin can send the X-Rebar-Token via its `header` config and reference infra/gerrit/webhooks.config, but this change removed that header from webhooks.config and established that the deployed plugin ignores arbitrary header keys.
scenarios: A developer maintaining the receiver reads these comments and believes Gerrit can/does authenticate via X-Rebar-Token in webhooks.config, contradicting the shipped auth path
advisory.suggested_fix: Revise the TOKEN_HEADER comment and _request_token docstring to state that the header/query token serves public /review/* callers, and that Gerrit's internal delivery is authenticated by the plugin's built-in X-Origin-Url header (per ADR-0014), not by a configured header.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the observability.sh offset-vs-counter delta restart-safe (e.g. treat a decrease as a counter reset and publish the new absolute value, or reset the offset file when the counter drops) so post-restart rejections are not silently dropped.
evidence: infra/scripts/observability.sh:222 `if [ "$review_webhook_auth_rejections" -ge "$review_webhook_auth_prev" ]; then`
infra/scripts/observability.sh:225 `  review_webhook_auth_delta=0`
infra/scripts/observability.sh:227 `printf '%s\n' "$review_webhook_auth_rejections" >"$REVIEWBOT_WEBHOOK_AUTH_OFFSET_FILE"`

src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:231 `_reset_webhook_auth_rejections` sets the attr to 0, and it is called in `lifespan` (app.py:262 in diff) on every process start — the offset file is not reset in lockstep.
advisory.finding: observability.sh delta computation can silently drop real webhook-auth rejections after a review-bot restart: the app resets its in-process counter to 0 on startup (app.py `_reset_webhook_auth_rejections` in lifespan), but the persisted offset file `/var/lib/rebar/reviewbot-webhook-auth-offset` retains the pre-restart high value. On the next probe, if the (reset) counter is below the stored offset the code takes the `else` branch and publishes delta=0 while overwriting the offset to the new lower value — so any rejections accumulated between the restart and that probe are never surfaced to the alarm.
scenarios: Token rotation misfires, bot rejects N Gerrit webhooks (offset climbs to N, alarm pages), operator restarts the bot which resets the counter to 0, the failure persists and new rejections accrue but stay below N until the counter climbs past the stale offset — alarm stays OK while LLM-Review silently starves.
advisory.suggested_fix: When `review_webhook_auth_rejections < review_webhook_auth_prev`, treat it as a counter reset and publish the full current value (`review_webhook_auth_delta=$review_webhook_auth_rejections`) rather than 0, before overwriting the offset file.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Document/harden the compose-network trust assumption for the tokenless `X-Origin-Url` path (e.g. restrict which containers can reach review-bot:8000, or note in ADR-0014 that any bridge-network peer can forge Gerrit origin).
evidence: src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:219-221 `origin = request.headers.get("X-Origin-Url", "").strip().rstrip("/") ... return bool(origin) and origin == cfg.gerrit_base_url.rstrip("/") and not forwarded_for`
gerrit_base_url default is a stable, guessable value: src/rebar/review_bot/config.py:280 `gerrit_base_url: str = "http://gerrit:8080"`
ADR text acknowledges the network boundary is the real gate (docs/adr/0014-inbound-webhook-auth.md) but the header check adds no cryptographic proof of Gerrit origin.
advisory.finding: The internal tokenless webhook path grants acceptance to any process on the docker compose network that can forge the `X-Origin-Url` header without `X-Forwarded-For`, widening the inbound trust boundary from `network-ACL + token` to `any compose-network peer`. `_is_internal_gerrit_webhook` requires only that `X-Origin-Url` equals the configured base URL and `X-Forwarded-For` is absent — both fully attacker-controllable by any container on the bridge network reaching `review-bot:8000` directly (not just Gerrit).
scenarios: A compromised or malicious sidecar/container on the same compose network posts spoofed patchset-created events with `X-Origin-Url: http://gerrit:8080` and no X-Forwarded-For, enqueuing bogus review work without any credential.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Do not authenticate the internal webhook path on client-controllable headers alone; bind the tokenless path to a verified peer identity (source IP/mTLS on the compose network) rather than a spoofable `X-Origin-Url`/`X-Forwarded-For` combination.
evidence: src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:219-221: `origin = request.headers.get("X-Origin-Url", "").strip().rstrip("/")` ... `return bool(origin) and origin == cfg.gerrit_base_url.rstrip("/") and not forwarded_for`
src/rebar/review_bot/config.py:280: `gerrit_base_url: str = "http://gerrit:8080"` — the value the `X-Origin-Url` header must match is a fixed, guessable, non-secret string, not a credential
src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:224-228: `_webhook_authorized` returns True from `_is_internal_gerrit_webhook` when the token compare fails, so a forged origin header fully substitutes for the token

src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:640-641: an accepted webhook `queue.put_nowait(payload)` enqueues attacker-supplied JSON for `voter.review_and_vote`, so the bypass reaches a state-changing sink (casting Gerrit votes)

src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:216: comment claims `Public nginx requests always carry X-Forwarded-For, so absence of that header keeps this fallback on the Gerrit-container path` — the guard is defeated the instant XFF is absent for any reason
infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template:66-71: the `/review/` block sets `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;` (append semantics) and sets NO rule clearing/overriding `X-Origin-Url`
search_files X-Origin-Url: no nginx `proxy_set_header X-Origin-Url` reset exists anywhere in `infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template`, so a client-supplied `X-Origin-Url` passes through nginx unmodified
advisory.finding: The new webhook auth bypass `_is_internal_gerrit_webhook` grants full tokenless access to `POST /webhook` based solely on client-controllable HTTP headers (`X-Origin-Url` matching a guessable non-secret value plus absence of `X-Forwarded-For`). Any client with direct network reach to the receiver (another compose-network container, an SSRF pivot, or any exposure of the loopback-bound port) can forge `X-Origin-Url: http://gerrit:8080` and omit `X-Forwarded-For` to inject arbitrary webhook events with no credential.
merged_from: The tokenless-path guard relies on `X-Forwarded-For` being absent to distinguish internal Gerrit deliveries from public nginx traffic, but nginx never strips or overwrites the inbound `X-Origin-Url` header on the `/review/` route. nginx only appends to `X-Forwarded-For` (`$proxy_add_x_forwarded_for`), so the entire public-edge protection collapses to that single header; there is no server-side validation that the origin header actually originated from Gerrit.
scenarios: A second container on the shared docker compose network (or a compromised one) POSTs to review-bot:8000/webhook with a forged X-Origin-Url and no X-Forwarded-For, injecting spoofed patchset events.
Any future misconfiguration that exposes port 8000, or an SSRF that can hit the loopback port, yields unauthenticated event injection.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Compare X-Origin-Url against Gerrit's canonicalWebUrl (a dedicated config/env value), not the internal compose REST base `gerrit_base_url`.
evidence: app.py:219: `origin = request.headers.get("X-Origin-Url", "").strip().rstrip("/")`
app.py:221: `return bool(origin) and origin == cfg.gerrit_base_url.rstrip("/") and not forwarded_for`
config.py:280: `gerrit_base_url: str = "http://gerrit:8080"` (the compose-network REST base; no GERRIT_BASE_URL override in the review-bot service env in infra/compose/docker-compose.yml)
infra/compose/gerrit.config:14: `canonicalWebUrl = https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/` — the value Gerrit puts in X-Origin-Url
Ticket RCA comment: 'the event processor sends built-in X-Origin-Url' — that header is the canonical web URL, not the internal REST base
blocking.finding: `_is_internal_gerrit_webhook` compares Gerrit's `X-Origin-Url` header against `cfg.gerrit_base_url`, but Gerrit's webhooks plugin sends X-Origin-Url as the canonical web URL (`https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/`), whereas `gerrit_base_url` is the internal compose REST base (`http://gerrit:8080`). They never match in production, so real Gerrit deliveries are still rejected — re-introducing the very bug the change fixes.
scenarios: Production: Gerrit posts patchset-created to review-bot with X-Origin-Url=https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/; comparison against http://gerrit:8080 fails; request 401s exactly as before the fix.
blocking.suggested_fix: Introduce a separate config field (e.g. `gerrit_canonical_web_url`, sourced from the deployed canonicalWebUrl) and compare X-Origin-Url against that, or match the origin's host/path against an allow-list that includes the canonical public URL.

blocking.finding: bugfix-size-attestation: this change touches 347 non-test line(s) — over the 150-line floor for a bug fix — but bug 073f-b86f-42c6-456f has no acceptable plan-review attestation (verdict: unsigned; no plan-review attestation record). A fix like this is a design change wearing a bug label: write the fix plan into the ticket's description, run `rebar review-plan 073f-b86f-42c6-456f` (it auto-escalates a bug with non-test file impact to the full review and SIGNS an attestation on a PASS; if the review passed but no attestation landed, `rebar sign-review 073f-b86f-42c6-456f` re-persists it cheaply, and `rebar review-plan 073f-b86f-42c6-456f --status` confirms it is current without an LLM call), then re-push.
